div.p: I used to think of a value in a PL as four things: a description, a name, an exp, and a val.

div.p: I want to be able to transform things in place using direct manipulation / PBD and have the states automatically stored into version history that is structure-aware.

div.p: E.g., I want to be able to directly manipulate a table in a spreadsheet to transform it, and then step through the states for just that table, and have it stored in a way that I can easily reuse the transformations or apply them to new data.

div.p: this the paper: A concurrent object is a data object shared by concurrent processes.

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: Linearizability is a correctness condition for concurrent objects that

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: exploits the semantics of abstract data types. It permits a high degree of concurrency,

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: yet it permits programmers to specify and reason about concurrent objects using known

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: techniques from the sequential domain. Linearizability provides the illusion that each

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: operation applied by concurrent processes takes effect instantaneously at some

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: point between its invocation and its response, implying that the meaning of a concurrent

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(224, 49, 49); color-scheme: light; interactivity: inert; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; row-rule-color: rgb(224, 49, 49); text-rendering: optimizelegibility;

div.p: object’s operations can be given by pre- and post-conditions.
